correctness.rationale: The integral identity D_n(X)=sum_j binom(n,j)^2 X^j(1+X)^(n-j), combined with Lucas congruences and Frobenius, gives D_{ap+b}(X)=D_a(X^p)D_b(X) (mod p), hence for each z in F_p the full base-p digit product. A single zero coordinate prevents the universal value-one property; otherwise digit vectors form a finite abelian multiplicative group H_p. Character orthogonality yields the exact count over p^k digit words; the identity digit v_{p,0}=1 makes all nontrivial character sums have modulus strictly less than |U_p|, giving the leading term and density zero. The finite semigroup generated by U is a group, hence any admissible prefix extends to a product-one word; the p-adic closure is the U-digit set of Hausdorff dimension log_p|U|. Independently computed full one-digit p×p value tables and generated group orders (1,4,6,10,144) for p=3,5,7,11,13, verifying U_13={0,4,6,8,12}, vectors v4=v8, exponent determinant -37 a unit mod 12, H13≅(Z/12)^2. Independent dynamic count gives C13(12)=8193. General Lucas/character proof is not replaced by finite checks.
residual_risks: Local group H_p not explicitly classified for all p>13; p-adic valuations beyond first power not claimed.
